<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s).

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx`  _(via chainField (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line; a string literal in refuseUnknownSealChainField), tenant_id (literal, a string literal in SEAL_DEFAULT_CHAIN_FIELD))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via tenant_id (literal, a string literal in SEAL_DEFAULT_CHAIN_FIELD))_
- `content/docs/deployment/seed-tenancy-repair.mdx`  _(via tenant_id (literal, a string literal in SEAL_DEFAULT_CHAIN_FIELD))_
- `content/docs/permissions/record-view-auditing.mdx`  _(via tenant_id (literal, a string literal in SEAL_DEFAULT_CHAIN_FIELD))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/config-resolution.mdx`  _(via tenant_id (literal, a string literal in SEAL_DEFAULT_CHAIN_FIELD))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via tenant_id (literal, a string literal in SEAL_DEFAULT_CHAIN_FIELD))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via tenant_id (literal, a string literal in SEAL_DEFAULT_CHAIN_FIELD))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via tenant_id (literal, a string literal in SEAL_DEFAULT_CHAIN_FIELD))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 17ed9e7bfd65532d83109273837e4a44624dee5c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b894101bf655f11deb19a66f2f88fea3bc5b3d7b` — the merge of head `31c51ed94a4abdddaff3156acfe50a22234a12ea` into base `17ed9e7bfd65532d83109273837e4a44624dee5c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b894101bf655f11deb19a66f2f88fea3bc5b3d7b && git checkout b894101bf655f11deb19a66f2f88fea3bc5b3d7b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 17ed9e7bfd65532d83109273837e4a44624dee5c 31c51ed94a4abdddaff3156acfe50a22234a12ea && git checkout -B drift-repro 17ed9e7bfd65532d83109273837e4a44624dee5c && git merge --no-ff 31c51ed94a4abdddaff3156acfe50a22234a12ea

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 17ed9e7bfd65532d83109273837e4a44624dee5c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 17ed9e7bfd65532d83109273837e4a44624dee5c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## L1: REWORK at `2cd55da5948dfe031efcb97e130af8fd6c1a6ff1` (2026-11-20T19:00Z). The run-time history is stated for one case of three, and ADR-0154 goes stale

**Scope.** I reviewed the 11 files against merge base `f44758b21e` (+352 / −76). The dev report is 7048006771. The claim is 7044270691, with amendments 7044528745 and 7048041398.

The rule, the pins, the doors and the narrowing record hold. Two things are owed: a changeset/entry correction, and an ADR record.

### What I checked

- **`sealChainColumnFaults`** (`object.zod.ts`).
  - It is one judgement for the named and the default column, built on #34351's predicates with nothing copied.
  - A missing column stops the judgement. A leaf-order column stops it too, which can never happen for `tenant_id`. A `valueFields` member and a non-text type are each a fault, in the old order.
  - The four named messages are byte-identical to main; I compared each `case` against the removed literals.
  - The default branch runs only when `chainField` is absent; a non-string `chainField` is left to the key's own type refusal.
  - The path is `['lifecycle','seal']`, and the fix names `organization_id` only where `resolveInjectedSystemColumns(object).tenant` holds. ✔
- **The premise.** `AUDIT_SEAL_DEFAULT_CHAIN_FIELD = 'tenant_id'` (`canonical.ts`), and the sealer's S3 reason fires on a chain column missing from `fields`. No non-test source outside `object.zod.ts` and the new entry declares `seal: {`, so nothing shipped is refused. ✔
- **Pins** (the new 34352 file). The refusal pins assert `code: 'custom'`, the path and the leading sentence. The opt-out pins assert that `organization_id` is *not* offered. The controls cover a text or lookup `tenant_id`, a named declared column, `organization_id`, and a named column beside a number `tenant_id`. There are two door pins: `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema` and `getMetadataTypeSchema('object')`. ✔
- **Ablations.** One leg per fault kind, red 5 / 6 / 1, with the controls green and a clean restore. ✔
- **Narrowing record.** The `!` title, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, the `minor` bump, and the ADR-0087 marker with its registered entry are all present. FROM/TO and the fix line are present. The `Skills-docs:` line names both skills files. The dogfood battery at this head shows 482 files and 4,098 tests with 0 failed. I accept the semantic entry's place outside the original surface, as ratified in amendment 2: the gate requires it. ✔
- **Docs and skills.** `objects.mdx`, the `chainField` describe, the regenerated reference, `lifecycle.md` (1,931 → 1,931 tokens) and eval case 16 now teach the refusal, and drop "parses but is not sealed" for a missing `tenant_id`. ✔
- **The sealer comment** is now true. ✔
- **CI at `2cd55da594`:** 20 success, 14 skipped, 37 in progress, 0 failed at my read. It is not yet green.

### Required

1. **The changeset says what run time did for case (a) only, and the entry's acceptance criterion is false for (b) and (c).**
   - The changeset says: "an object without a usable `tenant_id` parsed, and at run time the sealer reported it at `error` and sealed none of its rows."
   - That is true for (a), a missing `tenant_id`. It is not true for the other two cases (ADR-0154, the 2026-11-16 note):
     - **(b) a non-text `tenant_id`.** The sealer sealed the rows into the deployment chain with no report. The PR's own named-`chainField` message says so, and so does the entry's `reason`.
     - **(c) `tenant_id` in `valueFields`.** The sealer sealed the rows, carrying the committed value in clear as the chain.
   - Objects in (b) and (c) can therefore already have checkpoints. The prescribed fix for them changes the chain column, or changes its type. ADR-0154 measures what follows: the next pass re-seals the last sealed window, and `os audit verify` reports `listed_twice`. The entry's `reason` says this, but its `acceptanceCriteria` says "`os audit verify` still reports ok for objects that already had checkpoints". That holds for (a), which had none, and not for (b) or (c).
   - **Fix:**
     - In the changeset, state the run-time history per case, using the entry's own words for (b), and add (c).
     - Add one sentence to the fix line: on an object of case (b) or (c) that already has checkpoints, the fix re-seals the last sealed window, and verify reports it `listed_twice`.
     - Scope the entry's `acceptanceCriteria` to match.
2. **ADR-0154 is false at merge.** The 2026-11-16 note (`docs/adr/0154-…md`, the "It names a column that can carry an organization" bullet) ends: "The default `tenant_id`, when `chainField` is absent, is not judged at authoring; that half is #34352."
   - Amendment 7044528745 reads that sentence as "not made false". But it is in the present tense, and after this PR the default *is* judged at authoring.
   - **Fix (a record, not necessarily a file here):** the seat decides one of two things before landing. Either amend the claim to add one dated line to that note in this PR (the PR is already governed and Tier H), or file the ADR follow-up and link it from the PR body. Which one is not mine to choose.

### Not required

- `lifecycle.md` says "no text `tenant_id`". A lookup also passes, because it holds text, so the shorter wording is acceptable within the token ceiling.
- The out-of-scope finding (publish promotes a pre-landing draft unjudged) holds for every `ObjectSchema` refinement. Filing it is the seat's call.

### Before landing

- A delta L1 after items 1 and 2.
- CI green on that head.
- The CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER L2 PASS, same head (`packages/spec/src/**`, `skills/**`, narrowing).
- Tier H: maintainer approval through os-zhuang.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set change, one, a narrowing. On `main`, `refuseUnknownSealChainField` returned unless `seal.chainField` was a string. On this head an object whose `lifecycle.seal` has no `chainField` key is refused at `['lifecycle','seal']` when `tenant_id`:

No object and no deployment has an injected `tenant_id`, so "the registry injects it" is counted and is always false, as the tree says.
- (b) is declared with a numeric, boolean, date, datetime, JSON-shaped or multi-value type — RIGHT against scope addition 6917812639. On `main` such an object parsed and the sealer DID seal it, every row into the deployment chain, with no report (`chainValueOf` reads a non-empty string only). That is a refusal of something sealed, and it is the ruled one.

Named-`chainField` messages: byte-identical to `main`. I compared the four literals in the removed block with `namedSealChainFieldMessage` segment by segment; the only edit is the interpolated variable (`nonText` to `fault.type`). Path, code, order (not-a-field stops; leaf-order stops; then value-field, then non-text) and the two-issue case are unchanged.

Injected plan, default against named: both go through the one `sealChainColumnFaults`, so both read `resolveInjectedSystemColumns(object)` with no deployment and `injectedSystemColumnDefs(object)`. Doors — the tree's list is INCOMPLETE (S1). The changeset and the migration entry's `surface` name `os validate`, `os build` and the metadata save door. `ObjectSchema.create()` ends in `ObjectSchemaBase.parse` and `defineStack()` parses strictly by default, so both throw on this object. The PR's own fixture edit shows it: the `ObjectSchema.create()` probe in `object-lifecycle-seal.test.ts` had to gain a `tenant_id`. A code-authored stack is therefore refused when its config module is evaluated, not only on the three commands named.

False refusal — one class, undisclosed (S2). The sealer reads the REGISTERED field map, which has `objectExtensions` fields folded in; the parse reads the AUTHORED map plus the injected plan. An object that declares `seal` with no `tenant_id` and receives a text `tenant_id` from an `objectExtensions` entry parsed on `main` and, read in `plans()`, would be sealed. It is refused now. Read, not measured. #34351's named branch has the same reading, and `valueFields` has always been judged against the authored map.

Public surface: no export added or removed. `SEAL_DEFAULT_CHAIN_FIELD`, the fault type and the three helpers are module-private. The `chainField` `.describe()` gains two sentences, true on this head, and the regenerated reference page matches them.

### ② Semver level

A checkpoint's signed body carries its own `columns` set, so removing `tenant_id` from `valueFields` leaves earlier checkpoints readable under the set they were signed with; the `os audit verify` criterion is reachable. Its `surface` repeats the short door list (S1).

### ③ Boundary flags

ESCALATED to the seat as S4: it is "noted, not filed", and it holds for every `ObjectSchema` narrowing, so it needs a card.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` — holds. `sealChainColumnFaults` is one judgment for both branches and calls #34351's predicates (`resolveInjectedSystemColumns`, `injectedSystemColumnDefs`, `nonTextChainColumnType`, `isSealLeafOrderColumn`, the `valueFields` membership test); none is copied, and the old inline copy is deleted. The path `['lifecycle','seal']` for the default is the right node: no `chainField` was authored. Attempts to break it, all read in the code:

- injected `tenant_id` under some deployment: cannot exist (① a).
- lookup `tenant_id`: parses; `multiple: true` is refused as `lookup (multi-value)`. Both pinned.
- `tenant_id` in `valueFields` while `chainField` names another column: parses, as on `main`.
- no `lifecycle.seal`, `seal: null`, `chainField: null` or a number: no new issue.
- `chainField: ''`: named branch, refused as not a field, as on `main` (the sealer would read the default there; the parse refuses first).

`skills/objectstack-data/rules/lifecycle.md` — holds against the spec on this head. "Also refused: … no text `tenant_id` outside `valueFields` (or `chainField: 'organization_id'`)" is true; "Unsealed, `error` hourly: no declared `id`" is true (`sealedColumnSet` throws on an undeclared `id`, and the driver's `id` is not in the registered field map). The `os:check` example above it declares a lookup `tenant_id` and parses. See N1.

`skills/objectstack-data/evals/objects-fields-relationships.json` case 16 — holds against the prompt and the spec. The answer `seal: { valueFields: ['consent_text'] }` is unchanged; the sentence now says a text or lookup `tenant_id` is needed, that without it and without a `chainField` the object is refused at parse, and that a missing `id` still parses unsealed. Each clause is true on this head. The `must_contain` tokens are all still present.

`18.seal-default-chain-column-refused.ts` — agrees with the refinement (three cases, the path, the two fixes); see ② and S1.

`sealer.ts` — the comment is now true, and `plans()` is otherwise untouched: the `hasOwnProperty(fields, chainField)` report still fires for a raw registration and for a stored row loaded at boot. The pin `with no tenant_id field` in `audit-seal-sealer.test.ts` is unchanged. Done-when "the sealer keeps its runtime report" holds.

Tests — the 34352 file pins code, path and first sentence for (a), two opt-outs, six non-text types and (c), five controls and two doors. The two fixture edits add a `tenant_id` and assert the same outcome as before. Not pinned: `ObjectSchema.create()` and `defineStack()` as refusing doors (S1).

Changeset — judged under ②; see S1, S2 and N2.

Findings:

- S1 (should-fix) — the door list is short. The changeset ("The refusal fires wherever `ObjectSchema` parses: `os validate`, `os build` and the metadata save door") and the entry's `surface` omit `ObjectSchema.create()` and `defineStack()`, which throw on this object. For an upgrader with a code-authored stack this is the door that matters: the config module throws when it is evaluated, where on `main` the app loaded and the sealer reported hourly. Add the two doors to the changeset and to `surface`, and one door pin.
- S2 (should-fix) — a `tenant_id` (or a named chain column) that reaches the object only through an `objectExtensions` entry is refused at parse although the sealer, which reads the folded field map, would seal the object. The rule reads the authored map by design, as #34351 does; say so in the docblock and in the changeset's list of what is refused, with the fix (declare the column on the object itself). If the seat wants extension fields counted, that is a new card, not this PR.
- S3 (should-fix, carrier: seat) — file the add-only dated ADR-0154 note that records the default half as landed, so the 2026-11-16 note's two sentences stop reading as current.
- S4 (should-fix, carrier: seat) — file the draft-promotion gap: publish promotes a stored draft with no parse, so no `ObjectSchema` narrowing reaches a draft saved before it.
- N1 (nit) — `lifecycle.md` says "no text `tenant_id`" where a lookup is accepted too (its own example uses one), and offers `chainField: 'organization_id'` as if it were the only other column. The eval sentence has both right. Token headroom is 0, so a fix must trade words.
- N2 (nit) — the changeset's opening says the sealer "sealed none of its rows" for every refused object. That is case (a) only; (b) was sealed into the deployment chain and (c) per organization. The migration entry's `reason` has (b) right.
- N3 (nit) — the default message offers `organization_id` whenever the plan injects it, also where the author declared a non-text `organization_id` of their own. The `leaf-order` arm of the default message is unreachable and says so.

No must-fix.
